Tsunami-inspired long-wave modeling¶

Executed companion to the final V1.0 project report. Author: JIajun FU.

This notebook illustrates the verified solver and inspects the bundled final results. It does not rerun all expensive mesh studies. Models are one-dimensional, fully wet and nondispersive. The NOAA comparison is conditional on the documented geometry and input assumptions.

1. Mathematical model¶

Let $h=\eta-b>0$, $q=hu$, and static bed elevation be $b(x)$. The nonlinear balance law is $$h_t+q_x=0,\qquad q_t+\left(q^2/h+gh^2/2\right)_x=-ghb_x.$$ Linearization about a resting depth $D=-b$ gives $$\eta_t+(Du)_x=0,\qquad u_t+g\eta_x=0.$$ The report derives the finite-volume source balance, independent linear interface flux and restricted subcritical step coupling. A lake at rest must remain motionless.

In [2]:
grid = Grid(-1000., 1000., 300)
bed = -15 + 3 * np.sin(2*np.pi*grid.x/2000)
h0 = -bed
r = simulate_nonlinear_variable(grid, bed, h0, np.zeros(grid.cells), [0., 100.], SolverConfig(cfl=.4, boundary='periodic'))
rest_error = np.max(np.abs(r.eta[-1]))
print('Lake-at-rest maximum surface drift (m):', rest_error)
assert rest_error < 1e-10
plt.plot(grid.x, r.eta[-1]); plt.xlabel('Position (m)'); plt.ylabel('Surface drift (m)')
plt.title('Independent smoke check: lake at rest'); plt.grid(alpha=.2); plt.show()

Lake-at-rest maximum surface drift (m): 1.0658141036401503e-14

2. Aligned depth-step scattering¶

At 20 m to 5 m depth, the independent linear reference has reflection $R=1/3$ and transmission $T=4/3$. The hydrostatic control demonstrates that preserving rest alone does not ensure correct moving-wave transmission at a discontinuous bed. Bernoulli coupling is restricted to fully wet subcritical steps, with no head loss.

3. Shelf sweep and empirical resolution screen¶

$E=\|\eta_{NL}-\eta_L\|_2/\|\eta_L\|_2$. The mesh proxy $S$ is the sum of separate last-two-grid model changes divided by the fine linear norm. $E/S\ge5$ is an empirical screen, not a statistical confidence bound. The standard study has 18 cases; two failed weak-wave cases receive exploratory refinement to 16,000 cells.

4. Conditional laboratory comparison¶

The fixed Case A window uses G4 as incoming input and G5–G10 for comparison, without time shifts or parameter fitting. Archive and web metadata disagree on G4 position; the archive position 12.64 m is used and disclosed. Raw third-party measurements are not bundled; the supplied derived metrics can be inspected offline, while the full comparison fetches the official pinned archive.

5. Reproduce and interpret¶

Run python scripts/run_verification.py for all 35 tests and the analytical verification suite. Run python scripts/reproduce_all.py for the full computational workflow (internet is needed only to obtain the original laboratory archive). Open visualizations/wave_explorer.html directly for an offline interactive illustration.

The project supports a research-style computational report. It does not validate coastal inundation, wetting/drying, dispersive propagation or an actual historical tsunami. Nonlinear predictions do not uniformly improve the laboratory match. Read docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md and the final report before changing parameters.
